post.description: The single `merchant_callback_url` Binance calls for all events. RSA-signature-verified (no API key); dispatches on `bizType` — `TECH_PROVIDER` (authorisation) or `PAY` (order lifecycle). Unknown types are acknowledged so Binance stops retrying, but the event is dropped and alerted on as unhandled.

Order-status-change events for Binance Pay Onchain orders. SHA256withRSA-signature-verified against Binance's static partner public key (no API key); `X-BN-Connect-For` must name our partner code. Terminal-failure statuses fail the payment; success statuses record the reported withdrawal facts (the payment succeeds only after on-chain receipt verification).

200.description: Acknowledged (including event types and payloads this build cannot use)

500.description: Verification key/client unavailable or transient failure (Binance redelivers)

503.description: Webhook verification is not configured (Binance redelivers)

post.description: Order-status events for Bybit Pay PSP orders. Authenticated by the RSA-SHA256 signature over `timestamp + rawRequestBody` (headers `timestamp`, `signature`), verified against the public key pinned in configuration — there is no API key, and the in-request `publicKey` header is not trusted. A pay-order event is a trigger only: the order is re-queried from Bybit under our own credentials and the payment is driven from that answer (paid → succeeded; expired → the order is closed and the payment stays payable by another method). Every deterministic outcome is acknowledged with HTTP 200 and the plain-text body `success`.

200.description: Acknowledged — plain-text body `success` (including payloads this build cannot use)

401.description: Signature verification failed, or the timestamp is outside the accepted window

500.description: Storage failure, write contention, or an internal invariant violation (Bybit redelivers)

502.description: The order re-query to Bybit failed (Bybit redelivers)

503.description: Webhook verification or the Bybit client is not configured, or the configured key is unusable (Bybit redelivers)

CollectedData.description:
Inline Information Capture accepted at `/fetch`, in either shape:

- [`CollectedData::Structured`] — the typed [`StructuredIcInput`] schema, the format
  `/information-capture` uses and the one we are migrating to.
- [`CollectedData::Legacy`] — the `/confirm` array form
  (`{ fields: [{ id, value }] }`), accepted during the transition.

Disambiguated by serde: `StructuredIcInput` requires `fullName`/`dob`/`tosConfirmed`
while the array form requires `fields`, so the shapes never overlap. Both
normalize to the same [`IcData`] before screening.

Both shapes carry personal data and must never be logged in the clear.

Payment information (transaction hash). Present when status is
Succeeded, null otherwise.

Time to poll for payment status, in milliseconds. Not present if the
payment is in a final state.

expiresAt.description:
Optional custom expiration timestamp (Unix seconds since epoch).
Must be in the future if provided. If not provided, defaults to 15 minutes from now.

oneOf.description:
Optional per-payment settlement override (crypto destinations only).
Only honored for merchants with `enable_per_payment_settlement`;
replaces the merchant's offramp options. Each option is validated at
create time and rejected with a 400 if it violates any of: the asset
is supported, asset and destination are on the same chain, the
merchant has an MTA address on that chain, and the destination is
accepted by compliance screening.

PaymentFailureCode.description:
Machine-readable code identifying why a payment reached `Failed`.

Two distinct string forms exist per variant:
- **Strum** (`Display`/`AsRefStr`/`EnumString`): the DynamoDB storage form
  written to the `failure_reason` column. Preserves the existing on-disk
  value for rows written before this type existed.
- **Serde** (`Serialize`/`Deserialize`): the public API form. Deliberately
  decoupled from the internal term so that compliance-specific wording
  isn't surfaced to external consumers.

PaymentStatus.description:
Payment status representing the lifecycle of a payment.

Payments progress through these states from creation to terminal status.
Some states are specific to the payment source (pull vs push).

oneOf.description:
Machine-readable reason identifying why the payment failed. Present
only when `status == "failed"`.

Payment information (transaction hash, amount). Present when status is
Succeeded, null otherwise.

referenceId.description:
Merchant-provided reference ID for this payment, as supplied during
payment creation

oneOf.description:
Settlement metadata for the MTA → destination transfer. Null when
settlement has not completed yet (pending, non-MTA flows, or
pre-confirmation).

PaymentsSettlementInformation.description:
Settlement metadata returned for MTA-based payments.

Only present once the settlement transfer has completed on-chain.

oneOf.description:
Settlement success details. Null while settlement is pending,
populated once the on-chain transfer completes successfully.

PaymentsSettlementSuccessful.description: Details of a successful settlement transfer.

amount.description:
The settled amount — the asset/currency and value transferred. Read from
the confirmed on-chain transfer, falling back to the committed option
amount for test/APM settlements that move no on-chain funds.

txId.description:
Transaction hash of the MTA → settlement destination transfer. Optional
to leave room for future settlement shapes that may not carry one.

SettlementOverride.description:
Per-payment settlement override. Stored on the payment and used in both
the merchant API request and the DB; overrides always route through the
MTA, so unlike [`SettlementOption`] there is no `mta` flag to configure.

StructuredIcInput.description:
Typed Information Capture data — the JSON-schema shape used by
`/information-capture` and the format `/fetch` is migrating to.

Carries personal data (full name, date of birth, place of birth/residence), so
it must never be logged in the clear.

porAddress.description: Place of residence address. None when PoB-only

tosConfirmed.description: Whether the user accepted the Terms of Service

oneOf.description:
Commit the payment to `processing`. The `option_id` selects a
server-stored option; method and chain are derived from it. No
signature, hash, or relayer enqueue — test processing does no
on-chain work.

Mark the payment `succeeded`. Does not settle — settling is a separate
`settled` request. `tx_id` is the required, typed payment transaction,
recorded like any mined tx so downstream read surfaces (status, confirm)
can return it.

Mark the payment's settlement `successful` (sub-state of `succeeded`).
Not a [`PaymentStatus`]; the payment stays `succeeded`. `tx_id` is the
settlement transaction, required — the caller must supply one.

TestTransitionRequest.description:
Target state for a test transition. Tagged by `status`; callers supply
only caller-specific data — everything derivable (option data, payment
method, chain) is computed server-side from the committed payment.

TransferAction.description:
"Send this much of this token to this account" — the complete instruction, in
CAIP terms, with nothing to decode.

The other two actions describe a *transaction*: `walletRpc` names an RPC
method and its params, `build` carries an opaque payload to build from.
Both require the client to understand the chain it is on. A push payment needs
neither: the buyer sends a plain transfer from any wallet, and the only
information they need is the destination and the amount. Expressing that as
calldata would force every client to parse an ERC-20 `transfer` (and a
different encoding per chain family) just to display where the money is going.

Only returned for a push option, and only from `/fetch` — an option is never
quoted with one, because the destination does not exist until `/fetch` derives
it. It may be the only action returned: a Solana push option has no
transaction to sign.

amount.description:
What to send — the option's token and amount, repeated here so the action
is self-contained and can be rendered without cross-referencing the option
it came from.

to.description: The account to send to (CAIP-10), derived for this payment.

TxId.description:
Chain-agnostic confirmed-transaction identifier. Used only as the lifted id on
`CryptoTransferActionState::Confirmed` and in API responses — never an
in-flight state.

referenceId.description: Idempotency / reference ID provided at payment creation

isTerminal.description: Whether the payment has reached a final state

accountCaip10.description: Buyer address as a [CAIP-10](https://standards.chainagnostic.org/CAIPs/caip-10) account ID

fees.description: Fee breakdown derived from payment option data. Omitted when total fee data is unavailable.

percentage.description: Percentage fee component as a decimal percentage string, not a ratio. For example, "0.4" means 0.4%.

paymentUrl.description: Hosted payment page URL for this payment. The hosted page reflects the payment's current state.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the payment deadline, present only when the payment has an expiration

settledAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, present only when `settlement.settled` is `true` and a timestamp is available

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null if no more results

amount.description: Revenue amount in currency's standard unit

totalRevenue.description: Total revenue over succeeded payments, converted to USD. Always exactly one element — a merchant with no volume gets a zero rather than an empty array. Kept as an array for backwards compatibility.

value.description: Amount in minor units for the fiat currency
Amount in minor units for the token asset

MerchantPaymentSettlement.description: Settlement details. Omitted when settlement details cannot be reported yet. When present, `settled` is always included. When `settled` is `false`, no additional settlement fields are returned. When `settled` is `true`, `amount` is included and `txHash` is included when available.

amount.description: Net settlement amount after fees in the settlement unit. Present when `settled` is `true`.

txHash.description: Settlement transaction hash. Present when `settled` is `true` and an upstream settlement transaction hash is available.

from.description: Unit the payment was priced in

rate.description: How many whole `to` units one whole `from` unit converted into, as a decimal string

MerchantPaymentExchangeRate.description: Conversion applied between the payment unit and the settlement unit. Derived from the payment amount and the gross settlement amount (settlement plus fees), so it is the effective rate for this payment rather than a rate quoted independently. Omitted when the payment does not convert, or when the amounts needed to derive it are unavailable.

status.description: Refund state. "fully_refunded" is the only value this API emits.

fullyRefundedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the payment was fully refunded. Present only for fully refunded payments.

MerchantPaymentRefund.description: Refund details. Not currently populated: refund state is not yet projected into the payment read model, so this field is always omitted today. Reserved for a future release.
